decisions.reason: The old sole evidence s0250 explicitly has Ziyun as subject; it is the father's Liang-era promotion, not Qin's service. s0251 resumes Qin by name and gives his command; s0255 continues his promotions; s0258 names Qin relieving Nanzheng against Western Wei; s0261 records the court's further title and order. Read in their continuous Liang court context, these support Qin's existing served-Liang fact. Accept all four replacement citations, not a transfer of the father's office or dates to his son. Liang in the provincial office at s0255 is a province, not itself proof of the dynasty name.

sourceEvidence.zh: 幼而果決，趫捷過人。
sourceEvidence.literal: From youth he was resolute and decisive, swift and agile beyond others.
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: From boyhood he was bold and decisive, quicker and nimbler than other men.

sourceEvidence.zh: 宋末隨父子雲在洛陽，恒於市騎橐駝。
sourceEvidence.literal: At the end of Song he followed his father Ziyun in Luoyang and constantly rode camels in the marketplace.
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: At the end of the Song he followed his father Ziyun to Luoyang, where he often rode camels in the market.

sourceEvidence.zh: 後子雲還南，梁天監中以軍功至冀州刺史。
sourceEvidence.literal: Later Ziyun returned south; in the Tianjian era of Liang, through military achievement he rose to Inspector of Jizhou.
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: Ziyun later returned south and, through battle honors in Liang's Tianjian era, rose to Inspector of Jizhou.

sourceEvidence.zh: 欽兼文德主帥，征南中五郡諸洞反者，所至皆平。
sourceEvidence.literal: Qin also served as Commander of Wende and campaigned against the rebel cave-dwellers of the five southern commanderies; wherever he went all were pacified.
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: As Commander of Wende he campaigned against rebel cave tribes in five southern commanderies and pacified every place he reached.

sourceEvidence.zh: 欽有謀略，勇決善戰，步行日二百里，勇武過人。
sourceEvidence.literal: Qin had stratagem and plan, was brave, resolute, and skilled in battle; on foot he could cover two hundred li in a day; his courage and martial prowess surpassed others.
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: Qin was shrewd, bold, and a skilled fighter. On foot he could cover two hundred li in a day. His courage outmatched other men.

sourceEvidence.zh: 善撫馭，得人死力。
sourceEvidence.literal: He was good at soothing and controlling men and could obtain their death-effort.
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: He knew how to win men and call forth their utmost loyalty.

sourceEvidence.zh: 以軍功封安懷縣男。
sourceEvidence.literal: Through military achievement he was enfeoffed as Baron of Anhuai county.
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: For his military service he was enfeoffed as Baron of Anhuai.

sourceEvidence.zh: 累遷都督、梁南秦二州刺史，進爵為侯。
sourceEvidence.literal: He was promoted step by step to Commander and Inspector of both Liang and Nanchin provinces, and advanced in rank to Marquis.
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: He rose to Commander and Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin, and was promoted to marquis.

sourceEvidence.zh: 征梁、漢，事平，進號智武將軍。
sourceEvidence.literal: Campaigning in Liang and Han, when affairs were pacified he was advanced in title to Wise Martial General.
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: After the Liang and Han campaign he was promoted to Wise Martial General.

sourceEvidence.zh: 改授都督、衡州刺史。
sourceEvidence.literal: He was reassigned as Commander and Inspector of Hengzhou.
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Commander and Inspector of Hengzhou.

sourceEvidence.zh: 未及述職，會西魏攻圍南鄭，梁州刺史杜懷寶來請救，欽乃大破魏軍，追入斜穀，斬獲略盡。
sourceEvidence.literal: Before he could take up his duties, it happened that Western Wei attacked and besieged Nanzheng; Du Huaibao, Inspector of Liangzhou, came to request relief; Qin thereupon routed the Wei army greatly, pursued into Xie Valley, and slaughter and capture were nearly complete.
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: Before he could take up his post, Western Wei besieged Nanzheng. Liang Inspector Du Huaibao appealed for help. Qin routed the Wei army and pursued them into Xie Valley, slaughtering and capturing nearly all.

sourceEvidence.zh: 魏相安定公遣致馬二千疋，請結鄰好。
sourceEvidence.literal: The Wei Chancellor the Duke of Anding sent two thousand horses as a gift and requested friendly relations as neighbors.
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: Wei's Chancellor, the Duke of Anding, sent two thousand horses and sought peace between neighbors.

sourceEvidence.zh: 欽百日之中再破魏軍，威振鄰國。
sourceEvidence.literal: Within a hundred days Qin twice routed the Wei army; his prestige shook neighboring states.
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: Within a hundred days Qin defeated the Wei twice. His fame shook the neighboring states.

sourceEvidence.zh: 詔加散騎常侍，仍令述職。
sourceEvidence.literal: An edict added the title Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and still ordered him to take up his duties.
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: He was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and ordered to proceed to his post.

None of these four units has a pending translation proposal. Use separate reviewed non-temporal curation, not a fictitious translation-repair association.

decisions.reason: 使反 at s0031 means the messenger returned; that sentence reports Emperor Wu's order and does not evidence a rebellion. Chen Bozhi's rebel role is nevertheless supported by the surrounding sequence: he mobilizes under the Qi prince's purported order (s0032), has a letter forged and establishes an oath altar (s0034), takes the blood oath first (s0035), appoints his own subordinates (s0039), and is attacked by the emperor's army and flees to Wei (s0047). Accept the new evidence set while retaining the same role and subject. This does not make each appointment, in isolation, rebellion.

sourceEvidence.zh: 伯之謂繕：「今段啟卿，若復不得，便與卿共下。」
sourceEvidence.literal: Bozhi said to Shan: "This time I shall memorialize on your behalf; if I again fail to obtain approval, I will go downriver with you together."
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: Bozhi told Shan, "I'll petition for you this round. If the court refuses again, I'll rebel alongside you."

sourceEvidence.zh: 使反，武帝敕部內一郡處繕。
sourceEvidence.literal: When the messenger returned, Emperor Wu ordered that Shan be given a post in one commandery within the province.
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: When the messenger returned, Emperor Wu ordered that Shan be given a post in a commandery within the province.

sourceEvidence.zh: 伯之於是集府州佐史，謂曰：「奉齊建安王教，率江北義勇十萬已次六合，見使以江州見力運糧速下。
sourceEvidence.literal: Bozhi thereupon assembled the provincial and prefectural clerks and said: "By order of the Prince of Jian'an of Qi, I lead a hundred thousand righteous volunteers from north of the Yangtze who have already camped at Luhe; I am ordered to use Jiangzhou's existing forces to transport grain and descend swiftly.
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: Bozhi gathered his staff and announced: "By command of Qi's Prince of Jian'an, a hundred thousand volunteers from north of the Yangtze are encamped at Luhe. I am to mobilize Jiangzhou's forces, move grain, and march south at once.

sourceEvidence.zh: 我荷明帝厚恩，誓以死報。」
sourceEvidence.literal: I have received the thick grace of Emperor Ming and swear to repay it with my death."
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: I owe Emperor Ming a great debt and swear to repay it with my life."

sourceEvidence.zh: 使緭詐為蕭寶寅書以示僚佐，於聽事前為壇，殺牲以盟。
sourceEvidence.literal: He had Chi forge a letter from Xiao Baoyin to show the officials; before the reception hall they set up an altar and slaughtered a beast to swear alliance.
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: He had Chi forge a letter from Xiao Baoyin for the staff. Before the hall they erected an altar and cut throats to seal the oath.

sourceEvidence.zh: 伯之先歃，長史以下次第歃。
sourceEvidence.literal: Bozhi drank the blood-oath first; from the chief administrator downward they drank in order.
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: Bozhi swore first; the chief administrator and all ranks below followed in turn.

sourceEvidence.zh: 緭說伯之：「今舉大事，宜引人望。
sourceEvidence.literal: Chi urged Bozhi: "In undertaking this great matter, you should bring in men of reputation.
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: Chi advised him: "For an undertaking this large, you need men of standing.

sourceEvidence.zh: 伯之從之，仍以緭為尋陽太守，承忠輔義將軍，龍符豫州刺史。
sourceEvidence.literal: Bozhi complied; he moreover appointed Chi as Administrator of Xunyang, Cheng Zhong as Assistant Righteous General, and Long Fu as Inspector of Yuzhou.
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: Bozhi agreed. He made Chi prefect of Xunyang, Cheng Zhong an Assistant Righteous General, and Long Fu Inspector of Yuzhou.

sourceEvidence.zh: 武帝遣王茂討伯之，敗走，間道亡命出江北，與子武牙及褚緭俱入魏。
sourceEvidence.literal: Emperor Wu dispatched Wang Mao to attack Bozhi; Bozhi was defeated and fled, escaping by hidden paths north of the Yangtze; together with his son Wuya and Chu Chi he entered Wei.
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: Emperor Wu sent Wang Mao against him. Defeated, Bozhi slipped out by back roads north of the Yangtze and fled to Wei with Wuya and Chu Chi.

decisions.reason: 長子昭嗣 at s0186 says Zhao, the eldest son, succeeded. On c0926 the subject is Qingzhi (father) and the object is Zhao (son), so order 1 belongs on objectBirthOrder, not subjectBirthOrder. The reciprocal c0967 already places order 1 on Zhao as subject. Accept this single-key replacement, retaining biological parentage, people, evidence and all other fields. Current c0927 instead concerns the fifth son and must remain unchanged. No birth date or Yao kinship is inferred.

sourceEvidence.zh: 慶之性祗慎，每奉詔敕，必洗沐拜受。
sourceEvidence.literal: Qingzhi's nature was reverent and cautious; every time he received an edict he would wash and bathe before accepting it with a bow.
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: Qingzhi was reverent and careful. Whenever an edict arrived he washed and bowed before accepting it.

sourceEvidence.zh: 儉素不衣紈綺，不好絲竹。
sourceEvidence.literal: Frugal and plain, he did not wear silk brocade and did not love music.
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: He lived plainly, wore no silk, and cared nothing for music.

sourceEvidence.zh: 射不穿劄，馬非所便，而善撫軍士，能得其死力。
sourceEvidence.literal: His archery could not pierce a leaf; horses were not his forte; yet he was good at soothing soldiers and could obtain their death-effort.
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: He could not shoot an arrow through a leaf and was no horseman, yet he knew how to win soldiers' hearts and call forth their utmost loyalty.

sourceEvidence.zh: 長子昭嗣。
sourceEvidence.literal: His eldest son Zhao succeeded.
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: His eldest son Zhao succeeded him.

sourceEvidence.zh: 歷位雲旗將軍，安州刺史。
sourceEvidence.literal: He passed through offices to General of Cloud Banners and Inspector of Anzhou.
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: He rose to General of Cloud Banners and Inspector of Anzhou.

sourceEvidence.zh: 慶之第五子昕字君章，七歲能騎射。
sourceEvidence.literal: Qingzhi's fifth son Xin, styled Junzhang, at seven could ride and shoot.
sourceEvidence.idiomatic: Qingzhi's fifth son Xin, courtesy name Junzhang, could ride and shoot by age seven.

evidenceForAfter.idiomatic: His eldest son Zhao succeeded him.
